title: Fase E-2 (Father) — Versioned SQL-migration system replication (migrate.py + scripts/db/001_baseline.sql + slim init_db.py + tests), mirroring trade-ui Fase E-1 (handoff 58)
design_notes:
Fase E-2 replicates the versioned SQL-migration system (established on trade-ui in handoff 58 / Fase E-1, committed 3b686f1) onto the FATHER project. Same pattern, bigger scope (Father init_db.py was 5281 lines; after Fase F 59+60 removed ~823 lines of dead CREATE/seed it is now 4464 lines, 36 CREATE TABLE, 22 historical ALTER TABLE, 37 tables).

PROBLEM (same as E-1): no schema_migrations table means the system can't tell which schema version a DB is at. This caused the 2026-07-04 DB-loss incident (restore resurrected dead start_cmd/start_cmd_suffix columns because init_db.py re-ran CREATEs on restore). Fase F 59+60 ALSO showed the symptom twice: implementer ran init_db.py after a drop → recreated the dropped tables (init_db.py still had CREATE blocks) until the blocks were removed. A migration system makes schema evolution tracked/replayable/rollback-able and makes future drops SAFE reviewed migrations (00X_drop_*.sql) instead of migrate_c3_drop_dead_tables.py edits.

DESIGN (mirrors E-1):
1. scripts/migrate.py (new) — resolves DB via config.get_db_path(); creates schema_migrations table (filename UNIQUE, applied_at); discovers scripts/db/*.sql in numeric order; applies pending in a transaction with rollback on failure; idempotent (skips already-applied); exposes run_migrations(db_path=None) importable by init_db.py; __main__ entry.
2. scripts/db/001_baseline.sql (new) — all 37 current Father tables as CREATE TABLE IF NOT EXISTS, collapsing the 22 historical ALTERs into the current post-ALTER column state. No-op on the existing DB (tables already exist); creates everything on fresh. The 13 tables dropped in Fase F 59+60 are NOT in the baseline (already gone — pre-baseline history, like trade-ui's 7 collapsed ALTERs).
3. scripts/init_db.py slimmed — call migrate.run_migrations() for schema; KEEP idempotent INSERT OR IGNORE for canonical data seed (i18n 4-layer ui_text_slots/ui_text_slot_labels/ui_labels/ui_label_translations, endpoint_registry, bootstrap_dataset_registry, conventions, governance mappings, etc.); REMOVE inline CREATE TABLE + ALTER TABLE (now in baseline). Must remain backward-compatible: python3 scripts/init_db.py still works.
4. tests/test_migrate.py (new) — idempotency (run twice = 001 applied once); fresh-DB baseline creates all 37 tables; schema_migrations tracks 001 with timestamp; init_db.py end-to-end on fresh DB (schema + canonical seed); migration-failure rollback.

FATHER-SPECIFIC NUANCES vs E-1:
- seed_bridge.py EXISTS (20385 bytes) and runs AFTER init_db.py ("python3 scripts/init_db.py # schema + canonical defaults" then seed_bridge.py for bridge seed). E-2 MUST preserve this run order: init_db.py (now schema-via-migrate.py + canonical seed) → seed_bridge.py (bridge seed, UNTOUCHED). The slimmed init_db.py must not break seed_bridge.py's assumptions.
- Father DB is committed to git for rollback safety (per DB-loss incident). The migration system must work on the committed DB; migrate.py should create a timestamped backup before applying (as trade-ui's does).
- migrate_c3_drop_dead_tables.py (used in 59+60, SAFE_TO_DROP now 13 exhausted entries) becomes legacy after E-2 lands — future drops are 00X_drop_*.sql migrations. NOT in E-2 scope to remove it (separate follow-up); just note it's superseded.
- 001_baseline = CURRENT 37-table state (post-59+60 drops). 22 ALTERs collapsed. schema_migrations is metadata (only migrate.py + init_db.py read it).

REFERENCE IMPLEMENTATION: trade-ui (commit 3b686f1) has the proven E-1 implementation at /home/svend/trade-ui/scripts/migrate.py, /home/svend/trade-ui/scripts/db/001_baseline.sql, /home/svend/trade-ui/tests/test_migrate.py. The implementer MAY read these for reference (do NOT modify trade-ui).
